problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=-3xy.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=-6x{y}^{2}.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)>0?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.  Since we have strict inequality, we use dashed lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/2686a8ba9bdae16d92a184e7b35e856de2d031ce68be7f9262e4447ac3c74d04.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/8cc0734082fafe3628e1433f4c66c742858af51d95c8a068a4bd0025f0dc331a.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-6x$ | ${y}^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)>0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/896b351f836578ae08786cd22f94a30fd4e8c2d718197cd08d8dbbb0694a0f36.png)
